newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese T-bill yields to fall from Nov - Governor.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese T-bill yields to fall from Nov - Governor.

text.p: Interest rates on the Lebanese pound are following a downward trend and treasury bill yields will fall as from this month, Riad Salameh, Governor of the Bank of Lebanon, said in remarks published on Friday.
Salameh told the bi-monthly French-language magazine Le Commerce du Levant the central bank planned "a cut in interest levels on treasury bills as of November".
The Bank shaved t-bill yields for its weekly auction by between 0.03 and 0.05 percent on Monday.
Interest rates for the latest November 7 issue on the three-month, six-month, 12-month and 24-month treasury bills were 14.56 percent, 16.89, 17.75 and 21.58 percent.
Lebanon raised the rates last year, reaching 25.35 percent for three-month bills 37.93 percent for 12-month bills in September 1995.

Salameh said the Bank indicated the downward trend this year through a series of measures including cutting the repurchase agreement rate to 25 percent from 30 percent and reducing rates on certificates of deposit by three to four percent.
